brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: accessory:0#0,0#3 and accessory:2#0,0#3 (hex-acc-keyhole) are on the same back face of the bottom and top cells. Nothing checks how much load the hangers or wall screws can carry.

Five hex-acc-hook plates (10 hooks) are fitted at accessory:0#0,0#0, 1#0,0#0, 2#0,0#0, 1#0,0#1 and 1#0,0#5. The configurator only lets a cable coil, gaffer tape or FPV goggles hang on a hook, so I could only show a gaffer tape roll and a cable coil, not actual hand tools. The hooks have not been checked for strength or for the shape of real tools.
The open faces are capped and the joints locked. check_build passed with no rule errors and the mesh check clear. The build has 29 parts.

finish.summary: I built a wall tool rack: a column of three full hex cells (0,0) stacked as levels 0 to 2, held together with snaps. Two keyhole hangers sit on the back face (slot 3) of the top and bottom cells, so the rack lifts onto screws already in the wall. Five hook plates, two hooks each, are on the front and side faces: slot 0 on all three levels, plus slots 1 and 5 on the middle level. The other open faces are capped, I ran the joint lock, and check_build passed with the mesh check clear. To show it in use I hung a roll of gaffer tape and a cable coil on the hooks. The configurator only lets a cable coil, gaffer tape or FPV goggles hang on a hook, so I couldn't show actual hand tools hanging there. Two other placements were refused: a coil on the bottom front hook would hang down through the bench, and the top front hook was in the way of the tape below it. The configurator checks fit only, so I can't say how much weight the rack or the keyhole screws will hold.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
